title: Fixation Matters: Multidimensional Effects of Chemical Preparation on Morphology and SEM Image Texture Features of Extremophilic Bacteria
content:
Abstract
Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is widely used to investigate bacterial morphology and surface-associated features; however, sample preparation protocols may introduce artifacts that influence the interpretation of morphometric measurements and image characteristics observed in SEM micrographs. This issue is particularly relevant for extremophilic microorganisms, whose specialized cell envelopes may respond differently to chemical fixation. In this study, we evaluated two aldehyde-based fixation protocols (2.5% glutaraldehyde and Karnovsky's solution), each tested at three fixation times (1, 3, and 24 h) and with or without osmium tetroxide (OsO4) postfixation, in three Gram-positive bacterial strains: the polyextremophiles Exiguobacterium sp. S17 and Nesterenkonia sp. Act20 and the mesophile Kocuria rosea CH-021. Morphometric responses were assessed using cell surface area and surface-to-volume ratio (S/V), together with SEM image-texture analysis using Haralick-based features. Fixation conditions produced significant strain-dependent differences in both morphometric and image-texture outcomes. The magnitude of morphometric variability differed among strains, and SEM image-texture patterns were not always paralleled by morphometric measurements. These findings indicate that bacterial responses to fixation conditions are strain-dependent and support the combined use of cellular geometry and SEM image-texture descriptors for quantitative comparison of preparation conditions within a standardized SEM workflow.
